name: reachability
description: REACHABILITY ratchet. `tsc`, the test suite and every existing lint gate check TYPES and BEHAVIOUR; nothing checked whether a thing is REACHED. CLAUDE.md names 'built but unwired' as this repo's single most common defect, and every instance (services/lateFees, services/respa/earlyIntervention, calculateFlipAnalysis, taxSaleAuctions/taxSaleListings, achMandateSetup/achAutopayRun, rental_units.kind='pad', routes-contract-chain.ts, the rent-roll importer's unitKind arg) shipped GREEN and was found hours later by a manual audit. This converts that recurring audit into CI. Every count is strictly down-only, and raising one requires explicit founder/Iris-CTO sign-off (see lastBumpNote for the exceptions actually invoked): exports in server/services|jobs with no production call site; pgTables with no writer; pgTables with no reader; routes-*.ts never mounted; exports the gate cannot assert on because their module is dynamically imported in a way that hides which exports are touched; and service/job files nothing imports at all. The count of families is deliberately not stated here — it said 'four' for as long as there were four, and would have said it forever. THE CHEAPEST WAY TO SATISFY THIS GATE IS DELETION — the north star is a smaller codebase, and every reduction must be locked in by the commit that earned it (a stale-high baseline FAILS, same as `as-any`).

allowlist.reason: Read by compare-and-swap, not by SELECT. server/jobs/scheduler.ts acquires the single-flight lease with `UPDATE job_locks SET ... WHERE jobName = ? AND (expiresAt < now OR lockedBy = me) RETURNING id` — the WHERE clause IS the read and the RETURNING row is the answer. A separate SELECT-then-UPDATE would reintroduce exactly the race the lock exists to prevent, so this table can never grow a reader the linter's `.from(`/`db.query.` patterns can see. Structural blind spot, not dead weight.

Exported for the injectable-storage seam the module header describes; production consumes the singleton declared four lines below it (`export const investorVerificationService = new InvestorVerificationService()`), so the class has no EXTERNAL production consumer by construction and never can. It was not on this list before unit 53 for a reason worth recording: its only "consumer" was a STALE COMMENT — `// TODO(tsc): InvestorVerificationService exposes no listAllVerifications()` in routes-investor-verification.ts. This linter tokenises identifiers across production files and never distinguishes code from prose, so a comment naming a symbol makes it look reached. (The same mechanism, from the other side, is why scripts/check-org-scoped-fetch.mjs is now in SYMBOL_REGISTERS: its tenancy debt register named a module orphan and resurrected it.) Unit 53 deleted that TODO (it was false: the DB-backing wave HAD added listVerifications(orgId), which is now wired), and the deletion revealed the export. Deletion-revealed, not built-unwired — the same category the table-count notes below already carve out. Verified by re-adding the comment: the gate goes back to PASS at 654 with no code change.

The standalone negotiation copilot was KILLed and deleted 2026-08-13 (founder ruling; deletion-ledger row 'Negotiation copilot (standalone)'), and negotiationCopilot.ts was this table's only writer and only reader. The table is NOT dropped, deliberately: it holds customer negotiation sessions, and deleting customer data is a founder-only hard stop — so a DROP migration stays a decision someone makes on purpose rather than a side effect of a deletion wave. Retained here, not baselined, so the choice is visible in every gate run. When the founder authorises the drop, remove BOTH entries and lower both counts.

lastBumpNote: 2026-08-14, THE OPACITY RULE IS NARROWED — unreachedExports 580 -> 1439 and opaqueExports 984 -> 125. THIS IS THE ONE RAISE THIS RATCHET RESERVES TO SIGN-OFF, AND IT HAS IT: founder approval, picker, 2026-08-14 ('Approve the narrowing'). Nothing regressed and no code was deleted or added — the gate simply stopped exempting exports it never needed to exempt. WHAT CHANGED: a DESTRUCTURING dynamic import no longer makes a module opaque. `const { routeAITask } = await import('./x')` binds a bare identifier the usage tokeniser already sees, so exempting the module's OTHER exports on the strength of it was pure loss — that is how aiRouter.ts shielded ten exports occurring nowhere else in production because three siblings were destructured out of it. Of 1,244 distinct dynamic-import specifiers, 838 were reached ONLY by destructuring and 27 ever took a namespace binding, which is why 859 exports move in one step. A namespace binding, a `(await import(...)).default`, and a bare side-effect import ALL still confer opacity: this linter's bias is that a false OPAQUE is a miss while a false UNREACHED is an ACCUSATION, so anything not clearly destructured keeps its exemption. A TRAP CAUGHT DURING THE CHANGE, worth recording: the first implementation skipped destructured imports entirely, which also removed them from importedModules — and moduleOrphans jumped 45 -> 217, i.e. 172 modules that ARE imported were about to be reported as 'nothing imports this file at all'. A false accusation at scale. The two questions are now separate: EVERY dynamic import still marks the module imported (the module-orphan question), and only a non-destructured one marks it opaque (the symbol-exemption question). moduleOrphans is unchanged at 45, which is the check that the split is right. VERIFIED, not assumed: eight newly-unreached exports were sampled at random and every one has zero other production references. Among them are achMandateSetup and achAutopay symbols — which this linter's OWN HEADER names as canonical 'built but unwired' examples, and which its opacity rule had been hiding. PRIOR NOTE — 2026-08-14, B19 CLASSES 2+3 EXECUTED (founder ruling: 'Delete classes 2 and 3 now'). SIXTEEN module orphans deleted, 5,002 lines: authLockout.ts (class 2, superseded — middleware/authPathLimits.ts's loginLimiter is the live control, so this removed a DUPLICATE of a control and not a control); and class 3, the experiment family the 2026-08-01 deletion wave already ruled on once — delegationDepthV9, spendAutonomyV9, causalReasoningV9, playbookEvolutionV9, externalIntelligenceV9, compassAutoRecommendV9, scpCustomerLifecycle, scpExperimentEngine, scpSelfProvisioning, aiAdvisorTeamV15, agentTriggerMonitor, securityEnhancements, mobileEnhancements, marketplaceEnhancements, integrationEnhancements. Every one verified to have ZERO imports and ZERO mentions before deletion. CLASS 1 UNTOUCHED: breachNotificationTrigger, paymentApplication/, landlordCompliance, usuryCeiling, rental/leaseSigningPacket and the other regulated obligations stay — deleting those removes capability the product may be legally required to have, and B19 keeps them open as WIRING work. unreachedExports 651->580, moduleOrphans 61->45, opaqueExports 986->984, all locked in per the strictly-down rule. THE scp* TRAP WAS CHECKED FIRST, because this ratchet's own history records it: routes-scp-v2.ts is production-mounted and lazily imports FIVE scp modules (scpGoldenSuite, scpConfigVersioning, scpEvolutionEngine, scpMemorySystem, scpLLMJudges). The three deleted here are none of those. AND THE DELETION-REVEALED EXCEPTION AGAIN, invoked explicitly: tablesNoWriter 49->58, tablesNoReader 61->70. NINE tables lost their only writer, each traceable to a named deleted module — auth_fail_attempts (authLockout); agent_playbooks and playbook_evolutions (playbookEvolutionV9 — this note's prior edition explicitly predicted this, having recorded that agent_playbooks was NOT orphaned only because playbookEvolutionV9 still read and wrote it); compass_recommendations (compassAutoRecommendV9); spend_watchers and spend_optimizations (spendAutonomyV9); causal_investigations (causalReasoningV9); delegated_goals (delegationDepthV9); external_intelligence (externalIntelligenceV9). THE TABLES ARE NOT DROPPED — a production DROP TABLE is a founder-only hard stop — and all nine are hereby QUEUED for the founder table-drop decision alongside tax_strategies and tax_forecast_scenarios from B17 earlier today. See docs/company/deletion-ledger.md (2026-08-14) and BLOCKERS B19. PRIOR NOTE — 2026-08-14, B18 EXECUTED (founder ruling: 'Retire the dead duplicate'). unreachedExports 652->651: SECURITY_DEPOSIT_RULES and computeSecurityDepositDeadline (116 lines) removed from server/services/landlordCompliance.ts, which nothing imports. shared/regulatory/depositReturnRules.ts is now the single owner of security-deposit return deadlines. The two registries cited the same statutes and disagreed on FOUR states (FL 15 vs 30, ME 30 vs 21, MT 10 vs 30, OK 45 vs 30); removing the duplicate dissolves the disagreements rather than adjudicating them, because deciding which reading of a statute is right is legal judgement and a confident wrong deadline is worse than an honest gap — the live registry refuses a state it does not encode ({ known: false, unknownReason }). The removed function also parsed with a bare new Date() plus a NaN check, so 2026-02-30 became March 2 — the rollover defect unit 99 removed from everything live. ONLY THE DEPOSIT HALF WENT: landlordCompliance keeps its notice-period, retaliation, lead-paint, fair-housing and HAP-recert logic, which B19 classes as a regulated obligation built and never wired, where deletion removes capability rather than a duplicate. moduleOrphans stays 61 — the module is still there and still orphaned. Locked in per this ratchet's strictly-down rule; the run that caught it FAILED stale-high, which is that half of the ratchet working. See BLOCKERS B18 (coverage remains open). PRIOR NOTE — 2026-08-14, B17 EXECUTED (founder ruling: 'Delete the engine'). unreachedExports 653->652 and moduleOrphans 62->61: server/services/taxOptimizationEngine.ts (423 LOC) is deleted, and the STRING "taxOptimizationEngine" is removed from companyAgents.ts's ownedServices array — that string was the only thing outside the file that named it, and this linter counts string literals as uses, which is why a module fabricating tax figures was invisible to the gate built to find dead modules. It applied an invented 5% capital-gains rate to the thirty states missing from its twenty-state table and told callers those states 'tax capital gains as ordinary income' — false, because `undefined === 0` is false so an unlisted state took the else branch. Both reductions locked in per this ratchet's strictly-down rule. AND THE DELETION-REVEALED EXCEPTION, invoked explicitly: tablesNoWriter 47->49 and tablesNoReader 59->61. The deleted engine was the ONLY writer of tax_strategies and tax_forecast_scenarios (shared/schema/compliance.ts), so removing a dead writer made two transitively-dead tables VISIBLE — the increase is the gate WORKING, per the rule this note's prior editions established for exactly this case. Naming the deleted writer and queueing the exposed tables in the same commit is what that exception requires, and both are hereby QUEUED for the founder table-drop decision alongside the others already waiting. THE TABLES ARE NOT DROPPED: a production DROP TABLE is a founder-only hard stop. See docs/company/deletion-ledger.md (2026-08-14) and BLOCKERS B17. PRIOR NOTE — moduleOrphans SEEDED at 62 on 2026-08-14 — no existing baseline moved, and no new DETECTION either. These 62 files are already inside unreachedExports (228 of its 653 carry the [MODULE ORPHAN] label); what is new is counting them as FILES, because that is the unit the decision gets made in. 653 unreached exports is worked down one symbol at a time; 62 files totalling 19,685 lines that nothing imports is something someone can rule on in one sitting, and deleting one orphan removes several exports from 653 at once. CORROBORATION worth recording: an independent sweep written from scratch (import-specifier basenames + comment-stripped mentions, over all 888 server/services modules) returned the SAME 62. Two different predicates agreeing is why this number is trusted — the same sweep's FIRST run said 28 of 888 modules were imported, which was implausible on its face and traced to an import regex that forbade '{' between `import` and the specifier, excluding every braced import. IT IS NOT ONE DECISION. Three classes, and the file names tell you which: (1) REGULATED OBLIGATIONS BUILT AND NEVER WIRED — breachNotificationTrigger.ts computes GLBA 16 CFR 314.4(j), GDPR Art. 33 and state breach deadlines and its own header lists the five security events that should call it, and nothing does; paymentApplication/, landlordCompliance.ts (see B18), usuryCeiling.ts and rental/leaseSigningPacket.ts are the same shape. Deleting those removes capability the product may be legally required to have, so WIRING is the fix and where to hook it is a judgement call. (2) SUPERSEDED DUPLICATES — authLockout.ts is dead because middleware/authPathLimits.ts's loginLimiter is live; the control exists, this copy does not run, and deletion is correct. Do NOT read this class as a missing control. (3) EXPERIMENTS — the *V9.ts set, scp*, aiAdvisorTeamV15, *Enhancements.ts: the family the 2026-08-01 founder deletion wave already ruled on once. Full list and triage in BLOCKERS B19. PRIOR NOTE — opaqueExports SEEDED at 986 on 2026-08-14 — a NEW fifth family, and no existing baseline moved. These are the exports this linter has always admitted it cannot assert on, because a module that is dynamically imported ANYWHERE has every one of its exports exempted. Until now they were printed as an informational line with no gate, so the one population the gate cannot see was also the only one free to grow without limit. The clean example: server/services/aiRouter.ts is pulled in by `const { routeAITask, TaskComplexity } = await import(...)` from five call sites; those three names are genuinely reached, and the module's other TEN exports (MODEL_PRESETS, isClaudeModel, routeVisionTask, routeExtendedThinkingTask, getDbModelConfigs, applyEvalQualityGate and the rest) appear nowhere else in production source and are invisible purely because a sibling export is dynamically imported. One dynamic import launders every export in the module. Measured twice across the whole family — bare identifiers only, then permissively including `mod.symbol` property access, comments stripped both times because a comment naming a symbol makes it look reached (the mechanism this ratchet's InvestorVerificationService entry already records) — and both passes agree that effectively none of them occurs outside its own file. THE ROOT-CAUSE FIX IS DELIBERATELY NOT TAKEN HERE: opacity is applied per-MODULE while consumption is per-SYMBOL, and a DESTRUCTURING dynamic import needs no opacity at all since the destructured name is a bare identifier the usage tokeniser already sees. Of 1,244 distinct dynamic-import specifiers, 838 are reached ONLY by destructuring and just 27 ever take a namespace binding, so narrowing the rule would reclaim most of this family into unreachedExports — which would raise that number far above 653, and THIS RATCHET'S OWN RULE RESERVES RAISING ANY OF THE FOUR TO IRIS-CTO SIGN-OFF. So the definition is untouched and the blind spot is merely made countable and strictly down-only. Nothing was weakened. PRIOR NOTE — unreachedExports 654 -> 653 on 2026-08-13: VA task persistence (BLOCKERS B9, founder ruling). `services/vaManagement.ts` exported `generateTaskId` and `generateSopId`, which minted `task_<ts>_<random>` strings because there was no database to allocate an id — a fabricated identifier by construction, and unreached besides. Both are gone: ids are serial, allocated by `va_tasks`/`va_sops`. Against that, `createTask`/`updateTask`/`listTasks`/`getTask`/`verifyTask`/`listSops`/`createSop`/`toVaTask`/`toSop` are all newly exported AND all newly reached, so the count moved by the two deletions alone.
